title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 313: Rewilding the Mind: Ecology and Control
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 313 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

Rewilding the Mind: Ecology, Control, and Natural Process

Paragraph 1. For many years, park workers tried to keep wild parks very neat and tidy. In Europe and North America, rangers killed hunting animals, cleared dead wood, and dried wet land so parks looked pretty for tourists. However, nature writer George Monbiot says this strict control actually hurt nature. Parks looked clean on the outside, but many plants and animals disappeared.

Paragraph 2. Monbiot supports a different idea called 'rewilding'. Rewilding means stepping back and letting nature manage itself without human control. One key step is bringing back large wild hunters, such as wolves and wild cats. When there are no hunters, deer eat too many baby plants and stop young forests from growing back.

Paragraph 3. A famous example happened in Yellowstone National Park in 1995, when workers brought gray wolves back. Because elk were afraid of the wolves, they stopped eating near open rivers. Soon, new trees grew quickly along the riverbanks. The strong tree roots held the soil together, cooled the water for fish, and gave beavers wood to build ponds for frogs and birds.

Paragraph 4. Still, not everyone likes rewilding. Many sheep farmers worry that wild animals will hurt their traditional farm life, and some city offices prefer tidy parks that follow clear rules. Monbiot believes humans must learn to respect wild nature instead of controlling everything.

Complete the notes below.

groups.title: Questions 5–8
groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

steps: Đoạn 3: "...new trees grew quickly along the riverbanks."

q5.text: Why did rangers clear dead wood and dry wetlands in old parks?
options: A. To build large farms inside parks
B. To make scenery look neat for visitors
C. To help wolves hunt deer faster
D. To stop river floods during winter

steps: Đoạn 1: Để công viên trông gọn đẹp cho khách du lịch ngắm cảnh.

q6.text: What happens when all big hunting animals are removed from a forest?
options: A. Trees grow too tall for birds to nest.
B. Rivers freeze completely in summer.
C. Tourists stop visiting national parks.
D. Plant-eating animals eat too many young trees.

steps: Đoạn 2: Không có thú săn mồi, hươu nai ăn hết cây con khiến rừng không mọc lại được.

q7.text: How did bringing wolves back to Yellowstone help river fish?
options: A. New riverside trees shaded and cooled the water.
B. Wolves cleaned rocks at the bottom of the river.
C. Elk swam across the water less often.
D. Tourists stopped fishing near the valleys.

steps: Đoạn 3: Cây ven sông mọc lại, tạo bóng mát làm mát nước cho cá.

q8.text: Why do some city environmental offices dislike rewilding?
options: A. It costs too much money to plant trees.
B. It forces tourists to stay out of parks.
C. Wild nature is unpredictable and hard to control by rules.
D. Sheep farmers refuse to sell wool to cities.

steps: Đoạn 4: Các cơ quan thích công viên gọn gàng theo quy tắc rõ ràng hơn thiên nhiên khó đoán.
